definitions.explanation: The part of a plant that grows underground, absorbing water and nutrients.
The fundamental cause or source of something; the core or essence.

examples.english: Roots have started to come out.

examples.japanese: この{木|き}は{根|ね}が{深|ふか}い。
{花|はな}の{根|ね}に{水|みず}をやった。
examples.english: I watered the roots of the flowers.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}で{木|き}が{根|ね}から{倒|たお}れた。
examples.english: The tree fell from the roots in the typhoon.

examples.japanese: {雑草|ざっそう}は{根|ね}から{抜|ぬ}かないと、また{生|は}えてくる。
examples.english: If you don't pull weeds out by the roots, they'll grow back.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}の{根|ね}を{探|さぐ}る。
examples.english: To search for the root of the problem.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{根|ね}は{優|やさ}しい{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: He's a kind person at heart.

examples.japanese: {根|ね}も{葉|は}もない{噂|うわさ}を{信|しん}じてはいけない。
examples.notes: {根|ね}も{葉|は}もない = groundless, baseless

examples.japanese: {根|ね}から{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いて、{本当|ほんとう}の{原因|げんいん}を{見|み}つけよう。
examples.english: Let's listen from the root of the matter and find the real cause.
examples.notes: {根|ね}から = from the root, fundamentally

examples.japanese: この{問題|もんだい}は{根|ね}が{深|ふか}いので、{簡単|かんたん}には{解決|かいけつ}できない。
examples.english: This problem is deep-rooted, so it can't be easily resolved.

notes:
USAGE: {根|ね} refers to both literal plant roots and figurative foundations/causes. It's used in many idiomatic expressions.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{根|ね}が{深|ふか}い (deep-rooted)
・{根|ね}を{張|は}る (to take root)
・{根|ね}から (from the root, fundamentally)
・{根|ね}も{葉|は}もない (groundless, baseless)
・{根|ね}は (at heart, fundamentally)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{根|ね}{性|しょう} (nature, disposition)
・{根|ね}{気|き} (perseverance, patience)
・{根|ね}{元|もと} (root, base)
・{根|ね}{拠|きょ} (basis, grounds)
・{大根|だいこん} (daikon radish)
・{屋根|やね} (roof)

IDIOMS:
・{根|ね}も{葉|は}もない{噂|うわさ} (groundless rumor)
